whatServices.question: What data services does Cabana Data offer?
whatServices.answer: We offer end-to-end data solutions including Data Strategy & Consulting, Data Engineering & Architecture, Custom Application Development, and AI & Machine Learning Solutions. Our services are designed to help businesses at every stage of their data journey.

projectDuration.question: How long does a typical data engineering project take?
projectDuration.answer: Project timelines vary based on complexity and scope. A focused data pipeline project might take 4-8 weeks, while comprehensive data platform implementations can span several months. We work closely with clients to define realistic milestones and deliver value incrementally.

cloudPlatforms.question: Do you work with cloud platforms like AWS, GCP, and Azure?
cloudPlatforms.answer: Yes, we have deep expertise across all major cloud platforms including Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Microsoft Azure. We help clients choose the right platform for their needs and implement cloud-native data solutions.

industries.question: What industries do you serve?
industries.answer: We work with businesses across various industries including technology, finance, healthcare, retail, and manufacturing. Our data solutions are tailored to meet the specific regulatory requirements and business challenges of each sector.

security.question: How do you ensure data security and compliance?
security.answer: Data security is fundamental to our approach. We implement industry best practices for data governance, encryption, access controls, and audit logging. We also help clients meet compliance requirements including GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, and other relevant regulations.

personalytics.title: Crafting a One-of-a-Kind Media Planning Platform
personalytics.description: We designed the data architecture and reactive pipelines behind Personalytics — giving London Media a proprietary planning product powered by unified, real-time audience intelligence.

clientOverview.description1: London Media is a full-service media agency specializing in data-driven campaign planning and audience targeting for brands across Latin America. With a growing client base and increasingly complex data requirements, they needed a unified platform that could centralize media performance data and power smarter planning decisions.
clientOverview.description2: Personalytics is their proprietary media planning tool — built from the ground up alongside Cabana Data to transform raw audience and performance signals into actionable planning intelligence.

challenge.title: The Challenge
challenge.p1: London Media was operating across multiple disconnected data sources — ad platforms, CRM tools, spreadsheet exports, and third-party audience providers. Campaign planners spent hours manually consolidating data before any meaningful analysis could begin.
challenge.p2: The absence of a unified data layer made it impossible to build a reliable, real-time planning product. Personalytics needed a solid data foundation before a single feature could be shipped.
challenge.p3: The team needed a partner who could design the data architecture from scratch, integrate heterogeneous sources, and deliver a reactive pipeline that could power a product used daily by media planners.

approach.title: Our Approach
approach.description: Rather than patching over existing chaos, we built the data infrastructure Personalytics needed to be a world-class product.
approach.step1Description: We mapped every data source London Media relied on — ad platforms, audience providers, CRM exports — and defined a consolidation strategy that eliminated silos without disrupting existing workflows.
approach.step2Description: We designed a cloud-native data pipeline on Google BigQuery, ingesting real-time and batch data from 8+ sources into a unified semantic layer that Personalytics could query reliably.
approach.step3Description: With clean, structured data in place, we modeled the audience and performance entities that drive planning intelligence — giving media planners the signals they need, when they need them.

results.title: Results That Moved the Needle
results.stat1Description: Unify 8+ fragmented data sources into a single, queryable layer powering all of Personalytics's planning features.
results.stat2Description: Reduction in time spent manually consolidating data — from days to hours, freeing planners to focus on strategy.
results.stat3Description: Audience and performance signals now flow reactively into Personalytics, enabling live campaign adjustments without engineering bottlenecks.

impact.title: World-changer
impact.description: Beyond the technical delivery, this engagement redefined how London Media operates — and opened a new product category in the media planning space.
impact.impact1: Personalytics launched as a fully functional product, with a data layer capable of scaling to thousands of campaigns.
impact.impact2: Media planners reduced manual data work by 95%, shifting from spreadsheet consolidation to real-time platform interaction.
impact.impact3: London Media gained a proprietary competitive advantage — a planning product no competitor offers in their market.
impact.impact4: The pipeline architecture now supports multi-client deployments, turning a single project into a scalable product line.
impact.impact5: Data governance and lineage were established from day one, setting the foundation for future AI and ML capabilities.

takeaway.title: Key Takeaway
takeaway.p1: Personalytics didn't just need a dashboard — it needed a data product mindset applied end-to-end. By treating the data layer as a first-class product component, London Media was able to ship faster, scale smarter, and compete on a fundamentally different level.
takeaway.p2: The lesson is universal: before you can build intelligent products, you need intelligent data infrastructure. That's what Cabana Data delivers.
takeaway.highlight1: A product is only as good as its data foundation.
takeaway.highlight2: Reactive pipelines turn static reports into living intelligence.
takeaway.highlight3: Data architecture is a product decision, not a backend detail.
